kind: development-corpus measurement for #91; not a qualification and not a gate
question: Does context.line_counts, and then line_counts plus findings.citation_correction, change how many discovery sessions are lost to citation defects, at what token cost?

jobs.base: c1 profile: structured_output json_schema, max_output_tokens 20000, line_counts off, citation_correction off

model: spark/glm-5.3-flash only, LAN LiteLLM path; no paid model
corpus: evaluations/pilot, development split only; evaluations/holdout-v1 is not opened
budgets: ceiling 200000 per cell, so a 50000 grant per reviewer, as c1's aggregate arm; 1800 s session timeout; 6 turns
concurrency: 1 cell per job, the three jobs launched together: 3 cells and 12 streams in flight, c1's peak, with each job seeing the same engine load
sizing_rationale: Citation defects are rare: g2, s1, s2 and c1 lost 1 to 3 of about 144 discovery sessions each (about 1 to 2 percent).
Detecting a change in a rate that low needs thousands of sessions, which is days of the shared engine. This measurement does not try to; it sizes for the mechanism and for cost.

The aggregate arm is the cheapest cell with four evidence-v2 discovery sessions and no assessor, so it gives the most citations per token. Four defect cases, two of which (security-auth-order, tests-consumer-fixture) produced every recent past-end and placeholder-hash refusal, maximise citations per cell.
36 cells at c1's measured cell latency (about 600 s at this concurrency under load) is about 2 to 2.5 h of wall clock and about 2 million tokens, comparable to one c1 schedule.
Any correction offered will be observed with its outcome and token cost; the refusal-rate comparison between jobs is reported as counts with uncertainty, not as an effect.
launch: no idle-window rule (a measurement); concurrent load recorded before, every 15 minutes during, and in a full spend-log re-read after
spend_check: 0 LiteLLM fallbacks and every row served by the Spark deployment, from the spend log over the whole window
